per_window.ps-ns: dynamic_in_window in turns and near the chain ends, on a relatively rigid domain. RelaxDB source paper now read in full (Constantine et al. 1993; free isolated VL, 30 °C, pH 5.5, 50 mM deuterated acetate, 3.4 mM, 600 MHz): tau_r 8.45 ns; 15 amides need a nanosecond internal motion (tau_s 0.81-6.49 ns, mean amplitude S2s 0.85 +/- 0.13, largest cone angles at Gly-46, Gly-73, Lys-112 and Arg-113) and 15 more a picosecond one (mean tau_e 45 ps) (VL-J3); the remaining 59 amides are described by S2 alone, 0.72-1.00, with no enhanced fast motion (VL-J6, measured_not_detected).
per_window.us-ms: unresolved by the single-field Rex rule: 24 amides carry a significant exchange contribution to R2 (0.36-7.56 s-1; largest Thr-96, Ser-61, Gly-104, Trp-40 and Gln-6), including eight CDR residues, with the process bounded only between about 10-6 s and the 10-3 s CPMG refocusing period and no rate, population or Delta-omega (VL-J4). Six further residues with R2ex comparable to the error in R2 are kept as a suspected artefact (VL-J7). For five of the 24 sites the authors propose motion of nearby aromatic rings rather than of the NH vector.
per_window.slower_than_ms: unresolved: amide 1H-2H exchange rates from (3.7 +/- 0.6) x 10-6 min-1 (Tyr-91) to bounds near 3 x 10-2 min-1 at 22 °C in D2O, which the authors read as hydrogen bonding and burial rather than as the relaxation-active motions; hydrogen replacement, not a conformational opening rate (VL-J5).
per_window.undetermined: Crystallographic B-factors of VL inside the native and digoxin-bound Fab differ regionally, read by the authors as flexibility changes on VL:VH association or ligand binding (VL-J8, structure_only). From the 1994 abstract: the isolated VL self-associates weakly (Kd 2.5 +/- 0.7 mM) in a rapid monomer/dimer equilibrium, which is binding kinetics, not conformational exchange (VL-J1), and its solution fold matches the Fab/digoxin crystal VL to 1.05 A backbone RMSD with subtle differences in CDR2, CDR3 and strands A, F and G (VL-J2).

protein_summary.wt_apo_answer: Probably yes, without a rate: in the free isolated 26-10 VL at 30 °C, pH 5.5 in 50 mM deuterated acetate (600 MHz, single field) 24 backbone amides carry a significant exchange contribution to R2 of 0.36-7.56 s-1, concentrated at the chain ends, in the first strands and in all three CDRs (Thr-96 7.56, Ser-61 6.00, Gly-104 5.28, Trp-40 4.56 s-1); the authors place the motion between about 10-6 and 10-3 s but measure no rate, population or chemical-shift difference, propose nearby aromatic-ring repacking for five sites, and report no second set of backbone NH resonances. The sample is 3.4 mM and the domain self-associates weakly (Kd 2.5 mM), which may add to R2.
questions_for_gina: The 1993 source paper measures the free isolated VL at 3.4 mM, where the domain is partly dimeric (Kd 2.5 +/- 0.7 mM): should the atlas treat the R2 exchange contributions as a property of the monomer, or flag them as possibly raised by self-association?

The authors assign five of the 24 exchange sites (Cys-23, Arg-24, Trp-40, Gln-43, Phe-92) to motions of nearby aromatic rings rather than of the NH vector; should such side-chain-driven Rex count as backbone conformational exchange in the atlas?
protein_summary.buffer_note: The RelaxDB source paper was read in full on 2026-10-20 (case S6_r6_VL_20261020213928), superseding the abstract-only rows VL-VL_20261020152957-r1 and r2, which are no longer cited. Relaxation and hydrogen exchange come from different samples: 30 °C in 90% H2O/10% D2O for relaxation, 22 °C in nominally 100% D2O for exchange; the prose on p. 302 prints s-1 for two exchange examples where the methods and Appendix print min-1, and Gln-43 is printed inconsistently as an upper and a lower bound. The NOE values may be overestimated by about 0.1 through water presaturation and spin diffusion, 14 of the 103 HN correlations were too overlapped to fit, and with only three observables fast, nanosecond and us-ms processes cannot all be identified at one residue. The protein is 3.4 mM and in a rapid monomer/dimer equilibrium (Kd 2.5 +/- 0.7 mM), so minor aggregation may affect the global tumbling time; EDTA was removed and no phosphate or paramagnetic tag is present. The 1994 structure rows VL-r1 and VL-r2 remain abstracts. Second reads flagged no row in either VL case.
